messages:
maria: FYI ran a targeted p95 SLO-driven batchcrafting run this morning across route tiers (A/B/C). Captured kernel selection traces, KV cache hit/miss, queue depth histograms, and microbatch formation logs. Found a mixed bag of wins and a surprising regression on C-tier.

sam: can you drop the quick topline numbers? p95 before/after and any % diffs pls

maria: topline: A-tier p95 160ms -> 135ms (-16%), B-tier 210ms -> 205ms (-2%), C-tier 550ms -> 610ms (+11%). Token throughput improved for A/B, but C spiked.

maria: what we changed: switched to dynamic token budget targets per route tier (experimental):
```
dynamic_token_budget_by_tier = {"A":48, "B":24, "C":12}
batch_formation = "continuous_prefetch_v2"
queue_policy = "p95_latency_governor"
kv_prefetch = "prefix-length-heuristic"
```
We also enabled kernel fallback logic to prefer `fast-attn-int8` for short sequences; fallback to `fp16-cuda` if quant mismatch.

perfbot: perf summary (abbrev):
- A: p95 160->135, mean -12%, kv_hit_rate 78%->81%, avg_batch_size 6.3->7.9, kernel used: fast-attn-int8 82%
- B: p95 210->205, kv_hit_rate 66%->68%, avg_batch_size 4.8->5.2, kernel mix: fast-attn-int8 54%
- C: p95 550->610, kv_hit_rate 22%->18% (worse), avg_batch_size 9.1->10.4 (bigger batches but worse tail), kernel fallback events +34% (quant->fp16 switchover)

lee: hmm C-tier worse despite bigger batches. queueing seems longer so samples waited for token budgets to fill, then kernels fell back. Do we have per-request sequence-length distribution for C?

maria: yes — C has heavy long-context tails (many requests > 2k tokens). Our `dynamic_token_budget_by_tier` cap of 12 tokens ended up causing long requests to get undersized budgets, which pushed them into multiple batch cycles and triggered the kernel path that wasn't optimized for long-seq INT8, causing more fallbacks. Also KV miss rate dropped because prefetch heuristics didn't catch those prefixes.

anika: proposal: make token budget target a function of recent p95 and per-token processing cost estimate (observed kernel microsecond/token). Rough pseudocode: 
```
for each route_tier:
  per_token_us = rolling_mean(token_processing_us, 5m)
  target_tokens = clamp(ceil(p95_target_us / per_token_us), min_budget, max_budget_by_tier)
```
And add an override: if long_seq_fraction > 0.1 then prefer higher min_budget and aggressive KV-prefetch for that route.

frank: +1 on KV-prefetch. For long-context chat routes we should pre-warm KV for top-k recent prefixes: `prefetch_keys = recent_prefixes.sample(top=10, weight=recency)`; warm on enqueue. That reduces KV miss tail.

sam: question: how do we avoid blowing up latency for short requests in A-tier when we increase min_budget for C? We need per-route-tier isolation. Also need safe rollback if p95 regresses during canary.

lee: isolation is doable: runtime already supports route-based budgets + queue weight. We can add a hysteresis window to prevent oscillation: only change token budgets when p95 stays above/below threshold for 10 minutes and change magnitude < 2x. Also set `min_budget_by_tier = {A:12, B:8, C:24}` (note C higher) as a stopgap.

maria: I sketched a concrete config for the next canary (small weight to C-heavy traffic):
```
# canary config
batching:
  mode: slo_driven
  p95_target_ms_by_tier: {A:120, B:180, C:400}
  dynamic_token_budget:
    algorithm: p95_based_cost_est
    min_budget_by_tier: {A:12, B:8, C:24}
    max_budget_by_tier: {A:64, B:48, C:128}
  queue_policy:
    governor: latency_percentile
    hysteresis_minutes: 10
kv:
  prefetch: on
  prefetch_strategy: prefix_weighted_recency
  prefetch_topk: 10
kernelselection:
  prefer_quant_int8_threshold_tokens: 512
  fallback_grace_ms: 5
```
I'll push this to the canary group (10% traffic, C-heavy days) and collect p95 / kernel-fallback / kv-hit metrics.

perfbot: canary metrics to track (auto): p95, p99, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, avg_batch_size, queue_latency_p50/p95, cold_kernel_switch_count. will post trend graphs to the thread in 30m.

anika: also recommend adding an instrumentation trace to correlate kernel choice with batch composition: include batch_id, dominant_route_tier, avg_seq_len, kv_miss_count. that'll help debug C regressions faster.

frank: + action: implement prefix prefetcher as a background job that copies top-k prefixes into L2 cache 200ms before expected enqueue for streaming sessions. Will prototype.

sam: test plan before canary:
- unit tests for p95_based_cost_est algorithm
- offline replay on archived traffic with synthetic long-context amplification (~x3)
- perf smoke tests on canary infra (replicate kernel mix)
- alert if canary_p95 increases >5% within 15m window

maria: OK I'll open the canary PR and link replay artifacts. action items: PR for config + rollout, anika add trace fields, frank prototype prefetch, lee update governor hysteresis, sam watch canary alerts. I'll post status updates here. :rocket:

lee: thanks. if C still regresses we should consider splitting C into C1 (long-context) and C2 (short but heavy compute) routes so budgets are even more targeted.

maria: noted. will keep thread updated. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
